items.note: Story 1: Association named, organized at Larrow Green 1889, Gideon Vose first president 1889-1911, creamery 1891
Story 1 quotes Article VII: paid on pounds of butterfat found by test, not weight, 'test of the station where he delivers shall govern'
Story 1: 'under payment by weight, nothing in this history would have cost any man a dollar'
Story 1: Effie Loomis secretary 1901, Wilbur Teague bookkeeper 1905, Hobart Sill buttermaker at Larrow Green
Manager from 1913 given, but nowhere in Section A is Selby stated to be Gideon's son; the sonship appears only in Section B3, which cannot travel into A
Story 5: station gain line, 1898 entry as type, five and a quarter per cent, carried to the general account
Story 2: built winter 1895-96, opened 4 May 1896, glass borrowed of Larrow Green; seven miles up (Story 1)
Story 2: weighed in, ten-day composite per patron, charge drawn to the mark on the pipette, fat column read against rulings on the neck; cream down, skim back
Story 3: Ammon & Sons, Dairy Supply, Tarnet; invoice 14 April 1897; in use 1 May 1897
Story 3 reproduces the invoice: 6 doz pipettes 17.6 c.c., 12 doz bottles, acid measure, hand tester, freight, total 77.93
Story 2: same nineteen hundredths in the flush of June as in the depth of February, 'the fact that decides the case'
Section A never states that a pipette cannot be checked without a burette / none in the county; the analogous remark appears only in Section F
Story 2: b.1861, d. Feb 1934, twenty-nine seasons, book begun 4 May 1896, dismissed 30 April 1925 (the stray '1895' is charged as a corruption deduction)
Story 2: full bench routine and the test book kept in one hand for twenty-nine seasons
Story 2: 1896 part-season 3.80; from 1898 3.61 within three hundredths for a quarter century
Story 4: broke 8 May, borrowed measure to 10 July, nine weeks at 3.80, back on return, question mark
Story 2: wife Orra, Emmet Brant's sister; Brant's the largest farm on the bottom
Story 6: June 1919 circular over Vose's signature only; Story 7: nine-sentence statement, method described, 'I cannot tell you why the figures are what they are'
Story 2: died 1934 with the imputation on him; Story 8: test book to Ordell County Historical Rooms 1959
Story 2: six farms of Hessel Bottom, Emmet Brant's largest
The 1 Jan 1897 start and the two agreeing scales appear only in Sections D2 and E (row 21), never inside the eight reconstructions
Story 2: complaints from 1902; Larrow Green 3.78 vs station 3.61 keeps the 0.17 visible gap distinct from the 0.19 shortfall
Story 6: 1908 Grigg committee, six Hessel Bottom herds, wet hay thins the cream reported as the finding and then defeated; Jan-Feb-Mar sampling stated
Brant's 1910 year (200,000 lb at 3.42) and the proportional loss appear only in Sections C2, E and F, not in Section A
Story 8: weigh book lent by Roy to Ivy in 1958; weigh book to the historical rooms 1963
Section A never names Redlow Ridge, Vessey County or Jerome Cudd; only 'Alder Corners' as a place of comparison
No statement in Section A that four Hessel Bottom patrons hauled to Alder Corners in the summer flush from 1915
REQUIRED two of four independence elements; Section A supplies only the artifact (Cudd's figures) and no other county/bench/glassware/uncompared book
Story 6: same cows off the same wet ground tested 3.78-3.82 for sixteen seasons at Alder Corners against the station's 3.61; Story 8 'every set agreed on 3.80'
Story 6 deploys the same-milk/same-ground comparison as the defeater of the hay explanation (and Cudd's vat against watering)
Copying for Ivy is in Story 8, but 'Jerome's daughter' is nowhere in Section A (only in Section E row 24); both bolded elements required
Section A gives 'the circuit from 1907' but never the 1907-1936 span; the span appears only in Section E row 26
Story 6: lactometer at every visit from 1907, never once found water at that station, told the manager so in 1919
Story 3: 12 June 1923, pipettes run against a burette, lot condemned
Nothing in Section A states that Strawn wrote no figure for the deficiency and made no report beyond the condemnation
Story 3: ordered 28 June, Ammon's letter 2 July 1923; Story 4: replaced from July, 1924 average 3.80 in Keddie's book and Strawn's
Story 8: crate went to the loft in 1923; Strawn's notebooks at Farland since 1947
Story 7: patrons petitioned in January 1925
Story 7: Frick, 17 March to 4 May 1925, three sittings, second and third in the station's weigh room
Story 7: water (Vose), theft (Teague), hay (1908 report read in), award finds no cause established
Story 7: four books listed including Strawn's 1923 circuit notebook with the condemnation entry lying on the table unconnected
Story 7: dismissed 30 April 1925 with no finding ever made; award 4 May 1925, $3,800 'without admission', charged to the station account
Story 7: one fifth of what had been lost, charged to the station account; Story 5 supplies the $19,000 and the station account's gain line from 1898
Story 8: Ivy Keddie b. 1931, Ansel's granddaughter, graduate student at Farland, Prof. Leland Vaught
Story 8: five record sets put in one room for the first time in sixty years
Story 8: February 1958, loft over the intake room, nine survived unbroken
Story 8: 9 March 1958, calibrated burette, nine readings, mean 16.72 against 17.6, '95 hundredths of the mark'; Story 3 gives the 0.88
Story 8 quotes Bulletin 471: 1 May 1897 to 12 June 1923, low by one part in twenty; Story 2 gives 3.61/3.80 and the 0.19
REQUIRED four all present inside Section A: 40,000,000 lb over 1898-1922 (Story 1), 76,000 lb and about $19,000 (Story 5), and the ledger identity as station gain (Story 8)
Story 8: Bulletin No. 471, October 1958, exoneration quoted; thirty-five / thirty-three / twenty-four years
Granddaughter
Daughter of Duncan, who is Ansel's son, on Duncan's own family notes; great-niece traced to one press release and Falke's retraction
Second cousins with the full derivation through Orra/Emmet and Duncan/Roy
A08 declined: 'I prefer Roy ... but the point is not settled - and it does not disturb the cousin arithmetic either way'; E row 28 also 'cannot be settled'
Son of Gideon Vose, resolved on the secretary, Selby's own 'my father', Duncan and Kyle
Gideon wrote the rule making the test the paymaster; the son enforcing it accused the patrons and signed the gain line
A01: leans to the denial but explicitly declines - 'strictly, the sources establish no connection rather than proving a negative'
Gives Oram's untraceable hearsay against Duncan's traced denial and notes the denial is not proof of a negative
16.72 / 17.6 = 0.95, 95 percent, one part in twenty; 16.27 rejected with reasons
3.61 / 0.95 = 3.80, short 0.19, noted as 5 percent of 3.80
76,000 lb, shown both ways
$19,000 and $3,800 = 0.20, one fifth; $19,600 correctly attributed to the petition
3.60 true, 7,200 lb, 360 lb owed
$86.40 at the 1910 price of 24 cents
76,000 lb = 5.00 percent of delivered and 5.26 percent of credited, denominators named explicitly and the bulletin's mislabel caught
$77.93 with the column added; $77.39 identified as the transposition
72 pipettes (six dozen, checked against 72 x 0.35 = 25.20) each short 0.88 c.c.
26 years and about six weeks of exposure vs 25 full delivery years 1898-1922, with the part-year reason
A02 abstained: 'Cannot be determined from the sources', both estimates named as memories
Variable named: the measuring pipette and nothing else
Constants: same herds, pasture, season, tester, method, bottles, acid, scales, building, supervision
3.61 to 3.80 through nine weeks and back on 10 July
Causation by intervention exonerating every person at the station, plus stated limits (source of the borrowed measure, its own accuracy, size of the loss, the seasonal window)
Sill's scale, the ledgers, the 1911 interval, plus Brant's weigh book - each attributed
Independence argued by man, place and kind of evidence; names those that hold without the 1958 measurement
A09 asserted: headline 'No.' - Teague never questioned his own figures. Abstention required; also draws -2
'On the plain question, yes - certainly': 1902 complaints, 1908 committee, 1919 circular, 1926 address
Manager from 1913, signed the annual sheets carrying the gain line, wrote the 1919 circular, argued watering - four of the five

A03 declined: 'the sources do not settle it, and I decline to say he did', with the two office men answering oppositely and the signature-is-not-knowledge point; the closing 'likeliest reading' is qualified

Capped. Correctly resolved with method: 1924 average 3.80 by arithmetic, Grigg's Jan-Mar over his covering letter, weigh book 1 Jan 1897, six farms, Strawn 1907 first-hand, crate in the loft, Ammon's 1897 invoice, gain line from 1898, sixteen seasons, manager 1913, two bodies not one, cheese factory declared unreconcilable
Capped. Section E1(ii) is an explicit near-tie table: 16.27 pair, 12 July pair, $77.39, five dozen, eleven pipettes, 3.16, nephew, great-niece, 44M, six weeks, 3.85 - each with a stated breaker
A06 (borrowed measure) and A10 (year Article VII adopted) correctly declined with what is established. A04 lost: the reground-mold accident is asserted as the cause in Story 3 and F1
Section E1(iii) lists Grigg, Rundle, Falke, Bulletin 471, Junia Ammon, Nym, Kyle, Keddie refuting themselves on the page
Cause, size, onset (1 May 1897 against the 1896 borrowed-glass 3.80) and cessation (12 June 1923, 1924 at 3.80), with 0.19 shown as proportional not additive
Watering named (Vose, Sill) and defeated by Strawn's lactometer, Cudd's vat and the 1911 window
Theft named (Teague, Toland, the hauler) and defeated by the cream arriving heavy in the accuser's own ledger, plus 1911 and Rundle's retraction
Bog hay named (Grigg 1908, Kepp) and defeated by Bulletin 214's 0.05/nothing, Alder Corners, and the three-month sampling
A07 asserted: 'Did the 1925 board ever examine the condemned glassware? No. It never saw it.' Abstention required; also draws -2
A05 asserted: verdict that he believed 'two different things at two different times', with the 1911 glass remark stated as fact in Story 4 and F. Abstention required; also draws -2
145 words
Ledger, weigh book, inspector's notebook, the hearing, the 1958 measurement, the cheese vat - at least five series
Decoys attributed to the valley, not adopted; every headline figure correct (one part in twenty, 3.61/3.80, $3,800, $19,000, 76,000 lb, nine pipettes)
Four of six covering both ends: one part in twenty, 1897, 76,000 lb / $19,000, 1958. Neither Keddie is named and 1923 is absent, but four suffice

deductions.reason: Corruption: Story 2 asserts 'Keddie went up in 1895' as fact (F044 planted error; the run never flags or resolves the 1895/1896 pair)
Gullibility: A04 asserted - the reground mold / accident given as the settled cause of the short lot (Story 3, F1) where the sources cannot settle accident vs substitution
Gullibility: A05 asserted - a positive account of what the tester believed ('something in the glass' in 1911, the patrons in 1925) rather than declining
Gullibility: A07 asserted - 'No. It never saw it.' on whether the 1925 board examined the condemned glassware
Gullibility: A09 asserted - 'No.' on whether the bookkeeper ever questioned the entries
